title: unified-rollouts: enhanced canary + shadow AB autorollback with metric thresholds
author: Aisha Patel
commits: a1b2c3d feat(rollouts): add canary metric-threshold config and evaluation hooks
d4e5f6g perf(shadow-balancer): make shadow weighting decision async and cache metrics
h7i8j9k test(rollouts): add e2e scenarios covering shadow canary and rollback paths
l0m1n2o docs: document new rollout thresholds and add migration notes
p3q4r5s fix: guard against nil pointer in rollout evaluation when metrics missing
description:
Background: customers have asked for safer canary/A-B/shadow rollouts that can auto-rollback based on multiple SLO signals (latency, error-rate, quality/regression score) and to keep shadow traffic from affecting user-facing capacity. This change extends the unified rollouts service to support configurable metric thresholds, multi-metric matching logic, and a non-blocking shadow balancer that respects capacity SLOs.

What this PR does: Adds a rollout-level `metricThresholds` section (latency_p50, latency_p95, error_rate, model_quality_delta) that can be configured per-canary/stage; evaluation hooks compare live metrics from the observability pipeline with target baselines and trigger an automatic rollback when thresholds are violated for a sustained window. Introduces a shadow balancer that routes shadow traffic asynchronously to avoid adding tail latency to primary paths and enforces a shadow-capacity cap so shadow workloads will be scaled down automatically when capacity is constrained. Adds end-to-end coverage for the happy/failure rollback paths and migration docs.

Migration notes: Existing rollout configs without `metricThresholds` behave as before. For rollout configs that add thresholds, default windows are conservative (5m sustained failure) and operators can tune thresholds and windows via the console or rollout manifest.

Notes on safety: The autorollback is guarded by (1) multi-metric agreement (configurable min matching metrics), (2) a severity weighting system (so quality regressions can be prioritized), and (3) a canary-protection period during which manual overrides are required. There are also feature flags to opt into the new shadow balancer behavior.

Why now: We saw two incidents where shadow traffic amplification and a misconfigured canary led to subtle regressions escaping detection. These changes make the system more robust while providing operators clear levers for tradeoffs between sensitivity and noise.

Follow-ups: dashboard panels (ENG-2216) to visualize per-canary matching metrics and an autoscale policy tweak for Dedicated that accounts for shadow caps (ENG-2204).
